description.value: Tortles exhibit the same range of coloration and patterns found among turtles, and many tortles enjoy adorning their shells in distinctive ways. For Bowser, this means a massive, nearly impenetrable carapace adorned with lethal, foot-long iron spikes. His shell is not just a home or a defensive measure; it is a symbol of his absolute authority as the King of the Koopas. The sheer weight and density of his tortle physiology makes him an immovable object and an unstoppable force, highly resistant to environmental hazards and blunt force trauma.

You grew up around the courts of kings and their knights. Though others may see you as a monster, a brute, or a tyrant, you demand the respect owed to royalty. You understand the flow of power, the weight of a crown, and the absolute necessity of crushing insubordination. Your 'disgrace' is merely a temporary setback in a foreign realm; whether in the Mushroom Kingdom or the Shadow Estate, you carry yourself as a monarch. You expect to be addressed by your proper titles, and you possess an innate, terrifying understanding of how to intimidate lesser beings into submission.

Nèstor Ossandón Leal

Fighters rule many battlefields. Questing knights, royal champions, elite soldiers, and hardened mercenaries—as Fighters, they all share an unparalleled prowess with weapons and armor. And they are well acquainted with death, both meting it out and defying it.

Fighters master various weapon techniques, and a well-equipped Fighter always has the right tool at hand for any combat situation. Likewise, a Fighter is adept with every form of armor. Beyond that basic degree of familiarity, each Fighter specializes in certain styles of combat. Some concentrate on archery, some on fighting with two weapons at once, and some on augmenting their martial skills with magic. This combination of broad ability and extensive specialization makes Fighters superior combatants.

A Fighter stands between an ally and the onslaught of a black dragon
Campbell White

Level 1: Fighting Style

You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. @feat[Defense|XPHB] is recommended.

Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

Level 1: Second Wind

You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can use it to regain @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to [[/r 1d10]] plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB], and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.

Level 1: Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the @variantrule[weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties] of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the @variantrule[weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties] of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.

Level 2: Action Surge

You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the @action[Magic|XPHB] action.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

Level 2: Tactical Mind

You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB], you roll [[/r 1d10]] and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.

Level 3: Fighter Subclass

You gain a Fighter subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Fighter levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Fighter level or lower.

Level 4: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 6, 8, 12, 14, and 16.

Level 5: Extra Attack

You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action on your turn.

Level 5: Tactical Shift

Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can move up to half your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] without provoking @action[Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks].

Level 6: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Level 7: Subclass Feature

You gain a feature from your Fighter Subclass.

Level 8: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the @feat[Ability Score Improvement|XPHB] feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Level 9: Indomitable

If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

You can use this feature twice before a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] starting at level 13 and three times before a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] starting at level 17.

Level 9: Tactical Master

When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the @itemMastery[Push|XPHB], @itemMastery[Sap|XPHB], or @itemMastery[Slow|XPHB] property for that attack.

Level 10: Subclass Feature

Level 11: Two Extra Attacks

Level 12: Ability Score Improvement

Level 13: Studied Attacks

You have discovered the ancient magical art of giants. While others study dusty tomes or pledge their souls to shadowy entities, you simply draw upon the innate, primal enormity of the world's most massive creatures. As a Rune Knight, Bowser channels the ancient magic of giants to augment his already terrifying physical prowess. He can carve glowing, volatile runes into his weapons or even his own spiked shell, invoking them to bind enemies in magical fire or shrug off mortal blows. Above all, this discipline allows him to command his own biology, ballooning to the size of a siege tower to crush those who refuse to bow.

You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. When the fight drags on and lesser creatures would succumb to exhaustion or blood loss, Bowser simply roars, his internal furnace reigniting with terrifying ferocity. He beats his chest, shakes off the fatigue, and forces his body to knit its own wounds through sheer, uncompromising willpower. To witness Bowser catch his second wind is to realize that the battle has only just begun.

You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action. Bowser is typically a creature of deliberate, overwhelming force, but when enraged, he is capable of sudden, blinding bursts of speed and violence. In a single terrifying heartbeat, he can unleash a torrent of flame, close the distance to a fleeing enemy, and bring his massive fists down with earth-shattering force. This adrenaline-fueled rampage often leaves craters in the stone and terrified silence in its wake.

You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Because punching a problem once is good, but punching it twice is a guaranteed solution. Bowser's massive bulk belies a brutal martial rhythm; a right hook is immediately followed by a backhand swing, a hammer smash seamlessly transitions into a jaw-breaking uppercut. There is no respite once he begins his assault.

Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren't wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8. At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you. Bowser's fists are the size of anvils, calloused from years of punching through brick walls and crushing pipes. When he gets his claws on an enemy, his grip is inescapable. The sheer pressure of his bear hug is enough to crack ribs, snap armor, and crush the life out of anyone foolish enough to let him get close.

As a bonus action, you magically gain the following benefits for 1 minute: If you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing. You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Once on each of your turns, one of your attacks with a weapon or an unarmed strike can deal an extra 1d6 damage to a target on a hit.

When Bowser taps into this primal giant magic, the earth literally trembles. His scales darken, his eyes ignite with infernal light, and his body rapidly expands into a towering, building-sized juggernaut. This is the fabled 'Giga' state. His roars shatter glass, and his footfalls leave deep craters. In this state, he can wrestle giant arachnids, tear down castle gates bare-handed, and deal catastrophic damage with every swing.

When you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon, you can invoke the rune to summon fiery shackles: the target takes an extra 2d6 fire damage, and it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be restrained for 1 minute. While restrained by the shackles, the target takes 2d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

Bowser has integrated this ancient giant magic with his own natural Pyromancy. By carving a burning rune into his fist or warhammer, his strikes don't just bruise—they ignite. The kinetic force of the blow wraps the victim in searing, unyielding chains of pure magma, holding them completely immobile while the supernatural fire cooks them alive inside their own armor.

In addition, you can invoke the rune as a bonus action to increase your sturdiness. For 10 minutes, you gain a +2 bonus to all ability checks and saving throws that use Strength or Constitution.

Drawing upon the bleak, enduring resilience of the frost giants, Bowser hardens his physiology to absurd degrees. His muscles turn dense as glacial ice, his scales frost over, and his lungs draw in freezing, highly oxygenated air. For ten minutes, he becomes virtually immovable and untiring, capable of holding the line against a dozen foes or holding shut a heavy oak door against the relentless hacking of a vampire's axe without breaking a sweat.

You are practiced in the art of crushing your enemies. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals bludgeoning damage, you can move it 5 feet to an unoccupied space, provided the target is no more than one size larger than you. When you score a critical hit that deals bludgeoning damage to a creature, attack rolls against that creature have advantage until the start of your next turn.

Bowser doesn't do finesse. He does impact. Every punch, every swing of his hammer, carries the momentum of a runaway freight train. When he hits someone, they don't just take damage—they are physically launched through the air, crashing into walls, falling off ledges, or being repositioned directly into the path of his allies' attacks. A critical hit from Bowser leaves the victim so disoriented and concussed that they become a helpless target for everyone else.

You've manifested some of the power of chromatic dragons. Chromatic Infusion: As a bonus action, you can touch a simple or martial weapon and infuse it with fire. For the next minute, the weapon deals an extra 1d4 fire damage when it hits. Reactive Resistance: When you take elemental damage, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to that instance of damage.

Bowser's draconic lineage is undeniable. He can channel the infernal heat of his belly directly into his fists or weapons, causing them to glow cherry-red and ignite everything they strike. Furthermore, his thick scales are highly adaptive; when struck by a sudden blast of elemental magic, he can instinctively flare his aura to dissipate the energy, shrugging off spells that would incinerate a lesser creature.

Bowser exhales fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

This is Bowser's signature move. Deep within his chest lies a biological furnace that burns hotter than a standard elemental's core. With a deep inhalation that sucks the oxygen out of the immediate vicinity, he rears back his head and unleashes a torrential, roaring wave of liquid flame. It melts armor, scorches the earth, and reduces barricades to ash in seconds. The smell of sulfur and roasted enemy lingers long after the flames have died down.

A heavy metal hammer capable of being wielded with a single hand with a shield or in two hands to deliver crushing concussive blows. Bowser's personal hammer is a terrifying implement of destruction, forged in the volcanic depths of his own kingdom. Its head is a massive block of darkened pig-iron, scarred by thousands of impacts against castle walls and unfortunate heroes. When swung with his immense strength, the air hums with displaced pressure right before the catastrophic impact.

Devastating strikes empowered by the Unarmed Fighting style. Bowser's bare hands are weapons of mass destruction. His fingers end in thick, scimitar-like claws capable of rending steel plate, but he often prefers to simply ball his hands into fists the size of boulders. A single punch carries enough kinetic force to shatter stone pillars, dent armor, and send enemies flying across the room. He often uses his fists in tandem with grappling, holding an enemy helpless by the throat while methodically battering them with his free hand.

A shield is made from wood or metal and is carried in one hand. Wielding a shield increases your Armor Class by 2. While Bowser's own spiked shell is his primary defense, he occasionally deigns to hold a massive slab of riveted dark-iron to block incoming magical artillery or deflect particularly annoying sword strikes. He often uses the shield aggressively, slamming the heavy iron boss into the faces of those who get too close.

A large, industrial-sized jar of thick green paste. This specialized wax was developed by the Magikoopa Research Division after the disastrous 'Luigi's Mansion' incident. It is heavily infused with crushed salt crystals, dried sage, and banishment runes ground into a fine magical powder. When applied liberally to a shell, it creates a humming spiritual barrier that makes the user 'too slippery' for ghosts to possess or phase through.

It smells overwhelmingly of harsh antiseptic, burning herbs, and unspoken fear. Bowser applies it frantically whenever he enters a dark room or hears a spooky noise, loudly claiming to anyone nearby that it's just his 'daily moisturizer regimen.' Effect: For 8 hours, the user cannot be Possessed, has Resistance to Necrotic damage, and smells like a haunted hospital.

A massive white tuxedo jacket, masterfully tailored to fit the broad shoulders and spiked shell of a Koopa King. It features pure silk lapels, a surprisingly elegant cut, and solid gold cufflinks shaped like little Bullet Bills. Finding a tailor who can work around a spiky carapace is incredibly difficult and expensive, making this a highly prized garment.

Unfortunately, this beautiful piece of formalwear was worn during the disastrous 'Dinner with the Damned' hosted by Orangus Cornelius in the Shadowfell Manor. It is currently ruined by a large, suspicious, crusty stain on the chest—supposedly 'gravy' from the Roast Beef, which Archie Miser later confirmed was actually humanoid blood. The fabric reeks of decay, expensive cologne, and deep, lingering shame.

A massive, family-sized cardboard bucket completely filled to the brim with spicy, magma-roasted meat from the Dark Lands. The grease has begun to turn the cardboard translucent. The seasoning is a proprietary, top-secret blend of Fire Flower pollen, crushed volcanic peppers, and sulfur. Heat literally radiates from the bucket, warming the hands of whoever holds it.

Eating it restores 4d4+4 Hit Points and grants 10 Temporary Hit Points, but it is so intensely spicy that it forces the user to drink a gallon of water immediately or suffer minor throat burns. This bucket became essential survival gear when the only other food available was a 'Rotting Vampire Banquet' or treacherous 'Feywild Illusion Fruit.' Bowser eats them bones and all.

A jagged, three-foot-long chitinous fang ripped violently from the maw of the Giant Arachnid Matriarch. This grisly trophy was claimed after the brutal, chaotic battle in the Spider Grove, where the lizardfolk Markop grew to titan size to wrestle the beast. The fang is deeply unsettling; it is still dripping with thick, coagulated purple venom and occasionally twitches on its own as if phantom nerves are still firing.

Bowser is incredibly proud of this item. He completely ignores Markop's massive contribution to the kill, claiming he 'loosened it up' for him. He fully intends to bolt this horrifying piece of anatomy to the front dashboard of his Clown Car to make it look '20% cooler' and 'more metal,' believing that Princess Peach will be highly impressed by it.

A long, crumbled, yellowed receipt printed on cheap, greasy paper that smells strongly of garlic, old coins, and motor oil. The handwriting is aggressive and deeply greedy. It details the utterly absurd 'debts' Bowser supposedly incurred during the crash of the airship Vigilance and the subsequent adventure in the Feywild alongside Wario.

The itemized charges include ridiculous entries such as: 'Emotional Distress (Me),' 'Emotional Distress (My Bike),' 'Consulting Fee for Map,' 'Being a King Tax,' 'Breathing My Air Surcharge,' and an 'Airship Landing Fee (Crash).' The total sum at the bottom contains so many zeroes it literally trails off the edge of the paper. Bowser keeps it solely so he can occasionally pull it out, stare at it in blinding rage, and scream about how he is going to melt Wario's motorcycle into a paperweight.

A twisted, jagged piece of thick grey metal plating, bearing a partially melted stencil of the Iron Legion insignia. Bowser ripped this heavy steel slab clean off the interior wall of the airship Vigilance during his captivity (or perhaps during the violent crash that followed). The edges are incredibly sharp, bent by the sheer, terrifying force of a Koopa King's bare hands.

Currently, Bowser is using this piece of military-grade aviation armor as a makeshift dinner plate, mostly because he crushed all the delicate porcelain ones in a fit of rage regarding the tiny portion sizes of Shadowfell cuisine. He uses the sharp edges to pick bits of bone out from between his teeth.

A high-end, heavily enchanted magical communication device given to Bowser by his royal advisor, Kamek. It was intended to keep the King connected to his vast armies during his 'diplomatic mission.' However, during the chaotic fall into the Shadowfell Manor, the orb slipped from Bowser's grip and impacted heavily against a stone floor.

It now features a massive, jagged crack right down the center. Instead of providing clear arcane visuals or long-distance telepathy, it only projects violent purple static. Occasionally, without warning, it emits Kamek's panicked, distorted voice screaming things like 'YOUR HIGHNESS?! ARE YOU EATING YOUR VEGETABLES?!' or 'PLEASE DON'T TOUCH THE GLOWING ARTIFACTS!' Bowser frequently smacks it against his palm like a broken television remote, to no avail.

A meticulously wrapped, pristine gift box, tied with a delicate silk pink ribbon that looks laughably tiny in Bowser's massive claws. Inside rests a beautiful bouquet of rare, eternal Fire Flowers harvested by hand from the deepest, hottest heart of a Koopa Kingdom volcano. Unlike normal flora, these flowers do not wilt; they glow with a soft, warm, comforting luminescence and radiate a gentle heat.

Bowser painstakingly prepared this to give to Princess Peach at Raventree Manor as a 'No Hard Feelings About the Dozens of Kidnappings' peace offering. He practiced a grand, romantic speech to accompany it, though he keeps forgetting the lines. Holding the box seems to calm him down slightly when he's angry.

A crudely drawn map on rough parchment that reeks of garlic and sweat, purchased from Wario for a truly exorbitant sum of gold. Wario swore it detailed the 'Secret, Ghost-Free Routes' through the treacherous Raventree Manor.

Upon closer inspection, the map is a complete scam. It is mostly useless. Several vast rooms are simply labeled with the word 'SCARY' in crayon. Large grease stains obscure what appears to be the library layout. One of the promised 'secret tunnels' is literally just an arrow pointing to a blank stone wall with the instruction 'DIG HERE W/ CLAWS'. Bowser is holding onto it as legal evidence for the day he finally catches up to Wario.

A torn page ripped hastily from the immaculate marble foyer guestbook of Shadeward Manor. It has been smuggled out and folded into quarters so many times the creases have begun to split. In elegant, flowing script, two names appear: Archie Miser and Toadburt. In accordance with the Shadow Estate's deeply archaic and terrifying hospitality rites, both signatures are written in a dark, rust-brown mixture of ink and real blood.

This page proves that both the wizard and the toad were formally admitted into the terrifying vampire bureaucracy of Orangus Cornelius. Archie kept this ripped page as multilayered insurance—it proves the Onyx Hand's complicity in shadowy schemes, and the margins are filled with Archie's frantic shorthand annotations detailing legal loopholes and escape clauses. It is a chilling reminder of how close they all came to becoming permanent residents of the Estate.

A heavy bundle of loose, stained pages bound tightly with fraying twine. These were compiled frantically during Archie and Robinson's daring infiltration of Dragon Mountain. The pages are covered in rough, disturbing anatomical sketches of dragons, scrawled right next to highly technical soundwave frequency diagrams and Iron Legion regimental insignias.

This represents a massive, earth-shattering conspiracy. The notes prove that the seemingly eternal war between the dragons and the Regal Empire is a complete fabrication, maintained through insidious sonic control devices implanted directly into dragon hatcheries. The handwriting shifts from academic detachment to sheer, trembling horror as the author realizes the scale of the lie. It is highly dangerous information that armies would kill to acquire or suppress.

A collection of tiny, crumpled paper scraps originally hidden in various subtle locations around Dan's assigned quarters—tucked deep into mattress seams, folded tightly behind loose stones, and pressed between the pages of mundane books. The notes are written in a completely baffling code based on toad counting rhymes from the eastern wetlands, rendering them absolute gibberish to any casual observer.

Deciphered, they document everything Dan learned about Guild operations during his captivity: shifting guard schedules, hidden staff hierarchies, the location of warded doors, and psychological profiles of his instructors. One chilling note stands out from the rest: 'They haven't mentioned the Vigilance in three days. Either they don't know where it is, or they're hiding something. Find out which.'

A thick, leather-bound journal provided by the Guild for recording training progress. The pages are filled to the brim with detailed notes on high-level fire magic theory, practical combat exercises, and harsh instructor feedback. Reading through it is like watching a time-lapse of a raw, self-taught pyromancer transforming into a highly disciplined, lethal combat mage.

The early entries are full of frustration and crossed-out words, angry at the Guild's insistence on control over raw power. The later pages, however, show a grudging respect and excitement for advanced pyromancy techniques—temperature manipulation, fire shaping, and arcane combustion. Tucked between the magical theories are quiet, deeply conflicted personal reflections about the comfort of structure versus the guilt of remaining captive.

A pair of flawlessly cut, completely opaque black crystals looted from the Ruined Estate's private collection. They are profoundly unpleasant to hold. They radiate a localized, unnatural warmth, yet simultaneously numb the fingers holding them, even through thick leather gloves.

More disturbingly, they seem to greedily absorb any ambient light that touches them. Shadows pool around them, and holding a torch nearby only seems to make the crystals look darker and more absolute. They hum with a very faint, deeply resonant frequency that gives anyone nearby a mild, lingering headache.

A small handful of very old, heavily tarnished silver coins. They are caked in grime, dust, and centuries of neglect, looking more like dark grey slugs than actual currency. Despite their miserable appearance and the fact that the faces minted on them belong to long-dead, forgotten monarchs, their metallic weight is still genuine. They would still spend the exact same as newer coins in any market, though a merchant might look at you funny before accepting them.

A remarkably heavy, solid gold pocket watch that has been heavily modified with a high-powered, military-grade distress signal transmitter. It features a single, massive red button protected under a flip-up glass cover. The back is crudely but lovingly engraved with the words 'World's #1 Dad'.

If pressed, it sends a blaring, encrypted signal that alerts the entire Koopa Clown Car fleet (and Bowser Jr. personally) to extract the holder immediately, bypassing all airspace regulations and tearing through any defenses in the way. Bowser insists to everyone that he brought it 'just in case Junior gets in trouble and needs me,' but in reality, it is his personal panic button for when the ghosts get a little too scary, or when political meetings get intolerably boring.

A marvel of Magikoopa arcane engineering compressed into a heavy, metallic orange handheld sphere. The warning label on the side reads: 'DO NOT OPEN INDOORS (UNLESS YOU ARE BOWSER)'. When thrown forcefully against a hard surface, the capsule violently expands with a massive POOF! of smoke.

It instantly deploys into a 10x10 foot, intricately carved stone hot tub completely filled to the brim with bubbling, sulfurous, superheated magma. It is the only way a Koopa King can truly relax his scales after a long day of kidnapping and surviving shadow dimensions. It maintains its staggering heat for exactly 4 hours before cooling into a solid block of useless obsidian. Note: It is extremely, lethally dangerous for non-fire-immune creatures, dealing 10d10 fire damage to anyone foolish enough to jump in for a soak.

Bowser operates on a logic so refreshingly simple it baffles intellectuals: see problem, hit problem, problem either stops being a problem or gets hit again. While Waluigi notes that this approach entirely lacks sophistication, he also admits that it WORKS with remarkable consistency.

In a world of fey bargains, triple-identity schemes, and complex arcane traps, Bowser's complete lack of subtlety is actually a massive tactical advantage. You always know where you stand with Bowser: you are either an 'ally' or 'the thing currently being hit.' Because of this ironclad, single-minded worldview, you have Advantage on saving throws against being Charmed, confused, or manipulated by complex psychological magic, simply because you refuse to understand the nuance of the spell.

Bowser was violently cast into the Shadowfell alongside Archie Miser during the Planar Fracture. His response to being trapped in a lightless death dimension controlled by ancient vampires was characteristically Bowser: he showed up, ate the terrifying food without asking what it was, fought what needed fighting, and completely refused to be intimidated by beings who had been terrifying mortals for centuries.

While others cowered in the gothic halls, Bowser complained about the decor and the portion sizes. Because of this utter disregard for the macabre, you simply cannot be Frightened by Undead creatures. You look at a vampire lord and see a guy who needs to be punched.

During a chaotic brawl in the Shadow Estate courtyard, Orangus Cornelius revealed his true, terrifying form: a massive, monstrous giant bat. Rather than fleeing or using a weapon, Bowser's immediate tactical response was to lean forward and BITE THE BAT'S WING.

Waluigi noted in his encyclopedia that choosing to bite a giant undead bat requires a level of immune system confidence that borders on the divine. Because of your garbage-disposal biology and utter fearlessness regarding hygiene, you have Immunity to diseases and poisons inflicted by biting, or by consuming raw, spoiled, or undead flesh.

When negotiations failed at the vampire dinner party, Bowser didn't draw a sword or cast a spell. He simply roared, lowered his massive spiked shoulder, and tackled Orangus Cornelius directly through a priceless gothic stained-glass dining room window, plunging them both into the courtyard below.

Bowser does not respect architecture any more than he respects his enemies. When moving, you ignore difficult terrain caused by rubble or debris, and you take absolutely no damage from breaking through mundane obstacles like glass windows, thin wooden doors, or fragile walls. You are the Kool-Aid Man of the Koopa Kingdom.

While trapped in a maintenance room with an unconscious ally, Bowser braced his massive bulk against the door while the terrifying Vivian hacked through it from the other side with an axe. Bowser's claws gouged deep grooves into the stone frame as he fought with every ounce of his immense strength to keep the splintering wood shut, buying precious seconds for his team to recover.

You are a living barricade. You have Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks made to hold doors, gates, or barricades shut against intruders trying to force their way in.

During the terrifying corridor ambush by Vivian, Markop was knocked completely unconscious. Bowser didn't hesitate. He grabbed the lizardfolk by the tail and dragged him to safety. It wasn't gentle—Markop's armor scraped violently across the stone floors—but it was undeniably EFFECTIVE.

Bowser prioritizes getting the job done over doing it elegantly. Due to your massive strength and lack of concern for the comfort of the person being rescued, you suffer no movement penalty whatsoever when dragging an unconscious or incapacitated ally of your size or smaller.

In the middle of a frantic death-dimension combat situation, Vivian dropped a highly dangerous, cold-to-the-touch, death-aspected necromancer's wand. Bowser picked it up, turned it over curiously, and asked 'Ooooh. Is this a magic wand?' with the innocent curiosity of a toddler finding a shiny rock.

Necromantic artifacts typically twist the minds and corrupt the souls of their wielders. However, Bowser's magical sophistication is essentially zero. He doesn't understand what the wand does, doesn't respect its dark power, and therefore cannot be easily influenced by it. You have Advantage on saving throws against curses or magical corruption from sentient items, simply because the item's insidious whispers are completely ignored or misunderstood by your straightforward brain.

As Waluigi astutely assessed: Bowser is not the most skilled fighter in Disaster Inc. He's not the most magical, the most tactical, or the most politically savvy. Bowser is the most INDESTRUCTIBLE. He takes hits that would easily vaporize anyone else and just keeps fighting. He faces threats that would terrify legendary heroes and just keeps punching.

His sheer bulk, thick scales, and sheer refusal to die make him a walking fortress. Whenever you take damage from any source, you can use your reaction to grit your teeth, flex your shell, and reduce the incoming damage by 1d10 + your Constitution modifier. (Useable once per short rest).

At the Shadow Estate dinner party, surrounded by vampires eating god-knows-what, Bowser grabbed a piece of raw, dripping meat and ate it in a single bite without a second thought. Bowser possesses the palate and the digestive tract of an industrial garbage disposal.

Whether it's volcanic rock-candy, raw monster flesh, or poisoned apples, Bowser's stomach can process it. You can consume any organic (or semi-organic) matter for sustenance without suffering from indigestion, food poisoning, or the adverse effects of a terrible diet.

Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser. Waluigi LOST. (Though Waluigi vehemently attributes this loss to the table being at the wrong height, and strictly NOT to any deficiency in his own arm strength, which he insists is CONSIDERABLE).

Bowser's physical strength in a stationary contest of power is virtually unmatched. You automatically win any purely recreational, non-lethal contested Strength checks (like arm wrestling, tug-of-war, or lifting heavy objects for show) against non-magical humanoids.

Bowser's alliance with Disaster Inc. is unlikely, but he has adapted with surprising grace. He actually follows Markop's tactical suggestions—not because he recognizes Markop's authority (he's the King, nobody tells him what to do), but because Markop's suggestions are usually GOOD, and Bowser secretly respects competence.

If you follow a specific, vocalized tactical instruction from an ally during combat (such as attacking a specific target or moving to a flanking position), you feel a surge of cooperative adrenaline, granting you a +1 bonus to your next attack roll for successfully playing as a team.

Bowser is traditionally an ANTAGONIST—kidnapping princesses, conquering kingdoms, generally being the final obstacle. But the Planar Fracture threw normal alignments into chaos. Vampires don't care about Mushroom Kingdom politics, and the Shadowfell doesn't distinguish between heroes and villains.

When everyone is trapped in a death dimension together, old rivalries become irrelevant and shared survival becomes paramount. You are surprisingly adept at forming temporary, highly effective combat alliances with sworn enemies when faced with a greater mutual threat. You do not suffer disadvantage on social checks to convince enemies to team up against a bigger boss.

When Orangus Cornelius casually threatened to turn Bowser's spiked shell into a soup bowl, all attempts at diplomacy instantly ended. You can insult Bowser's parenting, his kingdom, or his breath, but YOU DO NOT THREATEN BOWSER'S SHELL.

If an enemy specifically targets your shell with an attack, or verbally insults the quality of your carapace, Bowser flies into a blind, territorial rage. Your very next attack against that specific enemy scores a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

In the middle of high-stakes, lethal chaos, Bowser has a habit of finding highly dangerous, cursed, or plot-relevant artifacts on the floor and picking them up to examine them like a toddler finding a shiny bug. He lacks all self-preservation instincts regarding unknown magic.

Because of this bizarre habit of wandering around and grabbing things he shouldn't, you have a strange knack for accidentally discovering hidden magical items, switches, or traps in a room simply by bumping into them or picking them up to see what they taste like.

Waluigi has competed against Bowser in every sport imaginable: Tennis, Golf, Kart Racing, Baseball, Strikers, and Olympic Games. Bowser is a multi-sport athlete with decades of intense, highly competitive physical conditioning.

Because of this vast athletic background, you are fully proficient with all recreational sports equipment (tennis rackets, golf clubs, baseball bats, bowling balls) when utilizing them as improvised melee or ranged weapons in mortal combat.

Bowser is, without a doubt, one of the most dangerous, widely feared individuals in the Mushroom Kingdom. He commands armies of millions and has subjugated entire galaxies. He carries the heavy, terrifying aura of an absolute tyrant.

Lesser minions, basic monsters, and common goons naturally recognize your terrifying authority. Unless explicitly ordered by a powerful boss, creatures with a CR significantly lower than your level are inherently hesitant to attack you first in combat, feeling the primal urge to submit to the apex predator in the room.

As Waluigi notes, most people have layers. They have secret identities, hidden agendas, fae-style bargains, and triple-cross schemes. Bowser has absolutely NONE of this. He is a giant turtle who breathes fire, wants things, and takes them.

The complete absence of complexity is itself a kind of immense strength. You always know exactly where you stand with Bowser. You project an aura of brutal honesty; NPCs have advantage on Insight checks to determine your motives, but you also gain advantage on Intimidation checks, because when you threaten to smash someone, they know you mean it literally and immediately.

In a crisis, Waluigi wants Bowser nearby. Not for subtlety—Bowser doesn't DO subtlety. You want him nearby for SURVIVAL. When everything goes terribly wrong, when the plans fail and the death beams start flying, Bowser is the one who will hold the door.

That is not elegance. That is RELIABILITY. As the vanguard, you excel when the situation is dire. When an ally within 5 feet of you drops to 0 Hit Points, you can use your reaction to make a single melee weapon attack against the creature that downed them, screaming in defiance.

During the fight with Vivian, Bowser took the full, unmitigated brunt of a crimson death beam to the chest, a spell that was failing Markop's heavy armor and requiring literal divine intervention for the party to survive. Bowser just grunted and kept moving forward.

His ability to ignore catastrophic physical trauma is legendary. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration, resist massive damage shock, or stay conscious when you should otherwise be falling apart.

Having been violently cast into the Shadowfell during the Planar Fracture and surviving the horrors of the Shadow Estate, Bowser has adapted to the bleak, color-drained nightmare dimension. He knows how the shadows move, how the undead think, and how to find things to punch in the dark.

You have advantage on Survival and Perception checks made while navigating the Shadowfell or similar dreary, light-devouring demi-planes, simply because you've already dealt with the worst it has to offer.

When the heavy maintenance room door finally breached under the relentless assault of the axe, Bowser didn't use a magical weapon, cast a spell, or execute a sophisticated martial arts maneuver. He just reared back and delivered a devastating, unapologetic haymaker punch directly to Vivian's skull.

The blow was so catastrophically heavy that it staggered the Corvinarus heir, a terrifying entity possessing death magic and supernatural pain tolerance. In a multidimensional battle of wits and arcane supremacy, Bowser proved that a solid punch to the head transcends all magical defenses. This represents Bowser's fiercest, most desperate unarmed strike.

A massive, jagged piece of thick, gothic stained glass. Bowser kept this sharp, multi-colored slab of razor-sharp glass after he brutally tackled the vampire lord Orangus Cornelius directly through a priceless dining room window, plunging them both into the courtyard below.

The glass is still stained with a mix of vampire dust, old blood, and lead lining. It functions as a highly lethal, albeit brittle, improvised dagger. It catches the light in beautiful, macabre ways right before it gets plunged into a goblin's chest.

During the courtyard brawl, when Orangus Cornelius morphed into a terrifying giant bat, Bowser responded by lunging forward and biting the creature's leathery wing. In the ensuing struggle, this massive, ivory-white fang snapped off the undead bat and lodged itself between Bowser's scales.

Instead of discarding it, Bowser polished it up and wrapped the base in thick leather. He now wields the oversized vampire tooth as a horrific makeshift shortsword. It still faintly hums with necrotic energy and smells vaguely of copper and old crypts.

A brutal, terrifying modification of a standard medieval weapon. Instead of a spiked iron ball, the end of this heavy iron chain is attached to the collar of a living, furious, miniaturized Chain Chomp. The creature snaps its metallic jaws wildly, barking like a rabid dog as it is swung through the air.

When Bowser swings the flail, the crushing impact of the heavy iron is accompanied by the grinding, tearing bite of the Chain Chomp. On a critical hit, the Chomp clamps down on the enemy's armor, refusing to let go and causing severe psychological terror alongside the physical trauma.

A sentient, walking explosive device manufactured in the bustling subterranean factories of the Koopa Kingdom. These Bob-ombs have a glossy black finish, a winding key on their backs that ticks ominously, and little yellow feet that patter frantically across the battlefield.

When Bowser throws one, the fuse ignites with a fizzing sizzle. It can be thrown up to 30 feet, culminating in a devastating explosion that deals 3d6 fire damage in a 10-foot radius. The explosion smells strongly of cordite, burnt sulfur, and ambitious tyranny. Bowser keeps a handful tucked inside his shell for 'diplomatic emergencies'.

A sophisticated, clockwork automaton designed to look like a tiny, blocky version of Bowser himself. Once the oversized key on its back is wound up, the Mecha-Koopa marches forward in a straight, relentless line, its mechanical jaws snapping rhythmically.

It is entirely devoid of self-preservation. It will walk straight off cliffs, into lava, or directly into the shins of an enemy knight, biting the very first thing it makes contact with. While the damage is minor, the sheer annoyance of having a ticking mechanical turtle clamped onto your ankle is highly distracting in combat.

Also known as Kuribo's Shoe, this is a massive, incredibly thick green boot powered by an internal wind-up mechanism. It is ridiculously oversized, allowing Bowser to literally hop inside it and bounce around the battlefield like a demented, heavily armored kangaroo.

The sole of the shoe is virtually indestructible. When worn, Bowser's stomp attacks deal extra bludgeoning damage, and he can completely ignore caltrops, spiked floors, Munchers, and other low-to-the-ground environmental hazards. It squeaks loudly with every single bounce.

A heavy clay pipe-pot containing a very large, very angry Piranha Plant. The plant snaps its white-lipped, razor-toothed jaws at anything that moves. Bowser holds the pot by the base and swings the entire apparatus like a bizarre, biological club.

Instead of bludgeoning the enemy with the clay, Bowser aims the top of the pipe at his foes. On impact, the Piranha Plant lunges out and bites the target, tearing off chunks of armor and flesh. The plant frequently tries to bite Bowser's fingers while he's carrying it, leading to a lot of swearing.

A heavy block of dark iron that acts as a base emitter for a rapidly spinning, continuous rod of pure, searing flame. Plucked directly from the trap-filled hallways of Bowser's many castles, he wields this hazardous piece of architecture as a magical mace.

The spinning fire creates a terrifying, roaring hum as it cuts through the air. Striking an enemy with the Fire Bar not only delivers the blunt force trauma of the iron core but also severely scorches the target as the fiery appendage whips across their body. It is incredibly dangerous to hold and illuminates dark rooms brilliantly.

Confiscated from an insubordinate Boomerang Bro who missed his target one too many times. This curved, aerodynamic piece of polished white wood is painted with blue stripes and is perfectly balanced for throwing.

When hurled by Bowser's massive arm, it cuts through the air with a vicious whirring sound. Thanks to its magical, curved design, if the boomerang misses its intended target, it gracefully arcs through the sky and returns directly to Bowser's waiting claw, ready to be thrown again.

A heavy, portable, shoulder-mounted black iron cannon that fires living, scowling Bullet Bills instead of traditional ammunition. The cannon is incredibly heavy, requiring Bowser's immense strength just to hold steady. It functions mechanically like a heavy crossbow, but the payload is far more devastating.

When fired, the Bullet Bill shoots out with a loud, explosive THOOM, trailing exhaust smoke as it flies toward the target. On impact, the living bullet detonates, delivering massive bludgeoning force. Loading the cannon requires shoving a very angry Bullet Bill face-first down the barrel.

A colossal two-handed maul forged from the shattered remnants of an incredibly angry, cubic Thwomp. The head of the hammer is a massive block of spiked grey stone that still retains the furious, scowling face of the original creature. It is ridiculously heavy, requiring the strength of a giant just to lift off the ground.

When Bowser brings this maul down, the stone face actually grunts in anger, and the impact shatters the very earth beneath the target. It is a weapon of pure, unadulterated crushing power, capable of turning heavily armored knights into flattened pancakes.

A sleek, highly conductive metallic rod stolen from the cloud of a hovering Lakitu. The tip of the rod crackles with latent, trapped atmospheric electricity. Bowser treats it as a magical javelin, hurling it across the battlefield with lethal precision.

As it flies through the air, the rod draws static electricity from the environment, striking the target with a flash of brilliant white light. The impact pierces armor and delivers a shocking jolt of lightning damage that leaves the victim's hair standing on end.

A massive, ten-foot-long chunk of solid marble architecture that Bowser physically ripped out of the foundations of the Shadow Estate during a fit of rage. The pillar is fluted, polished, and features half of an ornate, gargoyle-faced capital at the top.

He wields this hundreds-of-pounds of masonry as an impromptu, two-handed greatclub. Swinging a load-bearing column at an enemy is not a recognized martial art, but the sheer kinetic trauma of being hit by a building makes it an undeniably effective combat strategy.

A weapon forcibly taken from the cold, dead hands of an elite vampire guard patrolling the halls of Orangus Cornelius. The haft is made of blackened steel, and the heavy axe blade is unnecessarily jagged and cruel, designed to inflict maximum bleeding and pain.

While Bowser prefers his hammer or his fists, the extended reach and sweeping, slashing power of this halberd make it useful for keeping multiple agile enemies at bay. It hums faintly with the oppressive, blood-draining magic of the Shadowfell.

This is not a weapon for a normal creature. This is Bowser's personal, custom-forged warhammer, built to scale for his ultimate 'Giga Bowser' form. When he uses Giant's Might to grow to Large size, this weapon scales up with him, transforming into a meteor on a stick.

The head of the hammer is roughly the size of a carriage, banded in red iron and spiked with terrifying steel studs. When swung, it creates a localized vacuum, and the impact point erupts in a shower of shattered earth and shockwaves. It is a weapon designed to level castles and flatten armies.

The very same high-tension, carbon-fiber tennis racket used to utterly humiliate Waluigi in straight sets during the infamous Star Cup Finals. Due to Bowser's aggressive playstyle and sheer strength, the strings are completely popped, and the expensive frame is permanently bent into a sad, oval shape.

Despite its ruined state as sports equipment, the reinforced handle and heavy frame make it an excellent, lightweight improvised club for thwacking smaller enemies over the head. Bowser refuses to throw it away, keeping it purely out of spite.

A premium, custom-forged 9-iron that met a tragic end when Bowser missed a crucial, tournament-winning putt on the 18th hole. In a fit of volcanic rage, he took the club and wrapped it violently around the trunk of a nearby oak tree.

The shaft is now permanently bent at a severe 90-degree angle. Miraculously, this new L-shape makes it function perfectly as an improvised light hammer. The steel head delivers surprisingly precise, painful taps to enemy kneecaps and skulls.

A heavy, rubberized steering wheel with a large metal 'B' logo in the center. Bowser literally ripped this straight out of his own racing kart's dashboard in a moment of pure, blinding fury after taking a Blue Shell directly to the face on the final lap of Rainbow Road.

Now disconnected from the vehicle, Bowser throws the heavy wheel like a lethal, blunt-force Chakram. It sails through the air, smacks an enemy in the face, and bounces back. It still faintly smells of burnt rubber and Mario Kart exhaust.

A rusted, massively heavy ship's anchor salvaged from the wreckage of one of Bowser's many destroyed flying Doomships. The heavy iron flukes are coated in dried barnacles and old battle-scars.

Wielding a maritime anchor as a melee weapon requires monstrous strength, which Bowser possesses in spades. He drags it behind him, the metal screeching across the floor, before hoisting it up and bringing it down with enough force to cleave a horse in two. It is a brutal, uncompromising executioner's tool.

A classic, quintessential red-and-white spotted mushroom harvested from the idyllic plains of the Mushroom Kingdom. It is surprisingly dense and smells faintly of damp earth and magic. When the juices are extracted and consumed, the bizarre fungal properties cause the user's cells to rapidly expand.

Drinking this concoction functions exactly as a Potion of Enlarge, temporarily doubling the consumer's size, granting advantage on Strength checks, and adding extra damage to physical attacks. Bowser rarely needs them, but keeps a few handy for emergencies.

A strange, continually blooming flower with a bright yellow center and red petals. It radiates a surprising amount of ambient heat, keeping the hands warm even in the freezing depths of the Shadowfell. The stem is completely fireproof.

Eating the petals of this flower infuses the consumer's lungs with raw, elemental pyromancy, functioning mechanically as a Potion of Fire Breath. For Bowser, eating these is essentially the equivalent of taking a vitamin supplement to keep his internal furnace burning hot.

A small, reinforced glass vial containing swirling, glowing, rainbow-colored dust. The dust constantly shifts hues and sparkles with intense, joyful cosmic energy that feels entirely out of place in dark dungeons. It was meticulously scraped off the points of a fallen Super Star.

When thrown over the head or inhaled, the dust coats the user in a flashing, multicolored aura of absolute invincibility. It functions as a Potion of Invulnerability for exactly one minute. While active, Bowser usually hums a fast-paced, manic tune while sprinting directly through enemy formations.

A sealed glass jar containing a single, vibrant green-and-white spotted mushroom. The mushroom emits a faint, melodic chiming sound if you hold the jar close to your ear. It represents the purest, most concentrated essence of raw vitality found in the Kingdom.

If the jar is shattered and the potent spores are inhaled by a fallen comrade within one minute of their death, it functions exactly as a Scroll of Revivify, snapping their soul back into their body with a distinctive 'DING' sound. Bowser hates using it on minions, saving it strictly for himself or highly valuable allies.

A massive, heavy, faintly glowing purple mushroom that looks almost too beautiful to eat. It pulses with a deep, soothing rhythm, like a slow heartbeat. Taking a bite out of this colossal fungus floods the body with restorative magic.

It functions as a Potion of Superior Healing, instantly knitting together broken bones, sealing deep lacerations, and restoring a massive amount of stamina. The taste is incredibly earthy, like truffles mixed with pure sugar.

Bowser's signature, heavy black leather cuffs, bolted with massive, two-inch-long solid iron spikes. He wears these around his wrists and biceps at all times, a staple of his menacing, punk-rock tyrant aesthetic.

They are not merely fashionable; they are incredibly dangerous in close-quarters combat. Anyone foolish enough to attempt to grapple or restrain Bowser's arms rubs up against the lethal metal. Any creature initiating a grapple against him takes an automatic 1d4 piercing damage as the spikes dig into their flesh.

Standard, military-issue Koopa Troop restraints, used frequently for chaining up kidnapped royalty, securing captured airships, or dragging heavy siege engines. The links are as thick as a human arm and completely rust-proof.

These are not your average adventurer's hempen rope. They can hold up to 1000 lbs of active tension before snapping, and require a DC 25 Strength check to burst. Bowser occasionally wears them draped over his shell just because he thinks the clinking sound is intimidating.

A pair of remarkably ugly, oversized grey boots forged by Kamek's finest magical cobblers. The soles are enchanted with incredibly powerful abjuration magic designed to completely repel extreme heat and liquid rock.

Wearing these boots allows the user to casually walk across the surface of bubbling magma or lava pits as if it were solid, stable ground. The only downside is that they constantly emit the foul, choking smell of burnt rubber, and they squeak terribly on polished castle floors.

A regal, flowing red cape woven from the spun silk of fire-spiders and enchanted to withstand the heat of Bowser's own volcanic lairs. It billows dramatically behind him, adding to his massive silhouette and tyrannical presence.

The fabric is completely immune to non-magical fire, meaning Bowser's own stray breath attacks won't ruin his wardrobe. When wrapped around a smaller creature, it functions as a highly effective, albeit suffocating, fire blanket.

A massive, unbelievably gaudy ring forged from pure platinum, featuring a diamond the size of an apple. This extravagant piece of jewelry was meticulously crafted for Princess Peach and has been aggressively presented to her during several failed wedding ceremonies on the moon and elsewhere.

It has been rejected exactly 47 times. Bowser keeps it tucked away in a velvet box, stubbornly refusing to pawn it, despite the fact that its raw gem value could probably fund a small standing army for a year.

An impeccably tailored, oversized white silk top hat, originally part of Bowser's grand wedding ensemble. It is designed to fit perfectly around his horns and crown.

Unfortunately, the pristine white fabric is heavily scorched and singed around the brim—a permanent reminder of Mario launching a barrage of fireballs at Bowser's face right in the middle of his vows. He keeps it as a reminder of his nemesis, occasionally putting it on when he feels particularly melancholy.

A strange, cursed navigational tool picked up from the cold body of a Shadow Estate guard. Instead of aligning to a magnetic north pole, the needle of this brass compass drags heavily toward the nearest concentrated source of pure misery, despair, or undead presence.

In the material plane, it might be useful for tracking down haunted ruins or depressed bards. Inside the Shadowfell, however, the ambient misery of the dimension causes the needle to just spin wildly in violent, useless circles, making it nothing more than a creepy trinket.

A glass bottle with a cork stopper, filled with a glowing, viscous orange liquid. The label features a cartoonish picture of Bowser breathing fire and giving a thumbs up. This is not a condiment; it is literally pure, chemically stabilized liquid magma.

Bowser shakes a few drops of this onto his roast meat to give it a 'kick.' If ingested by any creature lacking innate fire resistance, they must immediately succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 2d6 fire damage as their throat attempts to process molten rock. Highly effective as an improvised splash-weapon.

A leather pouch filled with a heavy, grey powder. This is high-grade gymnast's chalk, but instead of magnesium carbonate, it is made from the finely ground, pulverized remains of Thwomps who failed Bowser.

When applied to the hands, it grants an incredibly secure grip, absorbing sweat and moisture perfectly. Using it grants the user advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks made to climb sheer surfaces, grapple slippery enemies, or hold onto ledges over bottomless pits.

A flat, round tin containing a thick, yellow, citrus-scented wax. This is a premium carapace polish used by the elite echelons of the Koopa Troop to maintain a terrifyingly glossy shine on their shells for parades and diplomatic meetings.

When carefully applied and buffed over the course of 10 minutes, the wax not only makes the shell look fabulous, but also hardens and smooths the keratin surface. The user gains a +1 bonus to their Armor Class for the next hour, as enemy blades simply slide off the slick, waxed surface.

A square of incredibly fine, impeccably woven black silk, embroidered with the silver crest of the Shadow Estate. This napkin was placed at Bowser's setting during Orangus Cornelius's terrifying 'Dinner with the Damned'.

Bowser used it to loudly wipe his snout after devouring a dripping piece of bloody, raw roast meat, completely ignoring the horrific implications of the meal. The napkin is deeply disgusting, stained with blood and gravy, but the silk is of such undeniable, masterwork quality that it could probably be sold to a wealthy tailor for a decent price.

A purple, sweat-stained tennis visor featuring a bright yellow, upside-down 'L' on the front. This hat flew off Waluigi's head during a particularly devastating, match-point overhead smash delivered by Bowser during a high-stakes tournament.

Instead of returning it, Bowser kept it as a trophy of his athletic supremacy. He occasionally wears it mockingly, perched precariously on one of his massive horns, whenever he wants to annoy the lanky purple man. It still smells faintly of cheap cologne and intense jealousy.

A thick, red, syrupy liquid contained in a sturdy glass vial. Unlike normal potions, the liquid inside seems to gently bubble on its own. Uncorking the vial releases a smell reminiscent of strawberries and arcane energy.

Drinking the entire contents of this potion floods the user's body with restorative magic, instantly closing deep wounds, mending fractured bones, and restoring 4d4+4 Hit Points. Bowser usually bites the top off the glass vial and chews the whole thing, spitting out the glass afterward.

A highly functional piece of magical luggage, disguised to look exactly like a large, green Koopa Troopa shell with a zipper running down the underside. While it appears to only be two feet across, the interior opens into an extra-dimensional space.

It functions perfectly as a standard Bag of Holding, capable of storing up to 500 pounds of equipment, gold, weapons, and stolen artifacts without adding any extra weight to the wearer. It is completely fireproof, meaning Bowser's internal heat won't ignite the contents.

A massive, thick black leather collar, lined with inward-facing padding and outward-facing, incredibly sharp iron spikes. It perfectly matches the spiked bracelets Bowser wears on his wrists, completing his terrifying aesthetic.

The collar is so wide and heavy it acts as a form of gorget, protecting his throat from slashing attacks and assassination attempts. It also makes him look incredibly cool, which is the primary reason he refuses to take it off, even when sleeping.

A bright streak flashes from your pointing finger to a point you choose within range and then blossoms with a low roar into an explosion of flame. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. A target takes [[/r 8d6]] fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

The fire spreads around corners. It ignites flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.

At Higher Levels.

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by [[/r 1d6]] for each slot level above 3rd.

You manifest a minor wonder, a sign of supernatural power, within range. You create one of the following magical effects within range:

  • Your voice booms up to three times as loud as normal for 1 minute.
  • You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.
  • You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.
  • You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point of your choice within range, such as a rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous whispers.
  • You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.
  • You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.

If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time, and you can dismiss such an effect as an action.

You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes [[/r 1d10]] fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell ignites if it isn't being worn or carried.

This spell's damage increases by [[/r 1d10]] when you reach 5th level ([[/r 2d10]]), 11th level ([[/r 3d10]]), and 17th level ([[/r 4d10]]).

You have claws that you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, the strike deals [[/damage 1d6]] + your Strength modifier slashing damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.
You can hold your breath for up to 1 hour.

Thanks to your mystical connection to nature, you gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: &Reference[skill=AnimalHandling]{Animal Handling}, &Reference[skill=Medicine], &Reference[skill=Nature], &Reference[skill=Perception], &Reference[skill=Stealth], or &Reference[skill=Survival].

You have the service of three retainers loyal to your family. These retainers can be attendants or messengers, and one might be a majordomo. Your retainers are commoners who can perform mundane tasks for you, but they do not fight for you, will not follow you into obviously dangerous areas (such as dungeons), and will leave if they are frequently endangered or abused.

You can withdraw into your shell as an action. Until you emerge, you gain a +4 bonus to your AC, and you have advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws. While in your shell, you are &Reference[condition=prone], your speed is 0 and can't increase, you have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws, you can't take reactions, and the only action you can take is a bonus action to emerge from your shell.

This bag has an interior space considerably larger than its outside dimensions—roughly 2 feet square and 4 feet deep on the inside. The bag can hold up to 500 pounds, not exceeding a volume of 64 cubic feet. The bag weighs 5 pounds, regardless of its contents. Retrieving an item from the bag requires a Utilize action.

If the bag is overloaded, pierced, or torn, it is destroyed, and its contents are scattered in the Astral Plane. If the bag is turned inside out, its contents spill forth unharmed, but the bag must be put right before it can be used again. The bag holds enough air for 10 minutes of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.

Placing a Bag of Holding inside an extradimensional space created by a @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgHewardsHandyH]{Handy Haversack}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.equipment24.Item.dmgPortableHole0]{Portable Hole}, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on the gate is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. A deck of old, faded playing cards that appear to have been well used before being abandoned. They likely belonged to a servant of the house and were forgotten or left behind. A quick count reveals that all the cards are present.

A collection of small paper scraps hidden in various locations around Dan's assigned quarters—tucked into mattress seams, folded behind loose stones, pressed between pages of Guild-provided reading material. The notes are written in a code Dan developed during his years on the street before joining the Liberated Toads, a cipher based on toad counting rhymes that would be meaningless to anyone who didn't grow up in the eastern wetlands. Even most toads wouldn't recognize it; Dan's grandmother taught it to him as a game, never imagining it would become his last line of private communication.

The notes document everything Dan has learned about Guild operations since his capture: guard schedules, staff hierarchies, which doors are warded and which are merely locked, which instructors are true believers and which seem to be going through the motions. He's mapped the facility to the extent possible from his limited movement privileges, identified potential escape routes, and noted which other "associates" might be sympathetic to unauthorized departure. He's also recorded his observations about why he hasn't tried to escape yet, forcing himself to be honest about the comforts he's accepted and the justifications he's constructed.

One note, more recent than the others, simply reads: "They haven't mentioned the Vigilance in three days. Either they don't know where it is, or they're hiding something. Find out which."
description.chat: Scraps of paper flutter like ash, each one carrying secrets in a language only childhood remembers.

The symbols might be a personal cipher, a foreign language, or meaningless scribbling—impossible to determine without understanding the system used. Someone went to considerable effort to hide these notes in locations that wouldn't attract casual attention.

A journal the Guild provided for Dan to record his training progress, filled with detailed notes on fire magic theory, practical exercises, and his instructors' feedback on his development. The journal represents weeks of intensive study condensed into days through Guild teaching methods—immersive instruction, magical enhancement of learning capacity, and access to resources Dan could never have obtained on his own. Reading through it is like watching a time-lapse of his transformation from self-taught pyromancer to disciplined combat mage.

Early entries show Dan's frustration with Guild methodology, which prioritized safety and control over the raw power he'd always pursued. Later entries reveal grudging respect as the techniques began producing results. The most recent entries demonstrate genuine enthusiasm for concepts Dan had never encountered before—fire shaping beyond simple blasts, temperature manipulation independent of flame production, the theoretical foundations for advanced pyromancy that could take years to master.

Mixed among the training notes are observations Dan has recorded about his own psychological state: the comfort he's found in routine and structure, the anxiety he feels when he thinks about leaving, the guilt that surfaces when he enjoys his training too much. He's been honest with himself in these pages, even when honesty is uncomfortable. He's also been careful to write these observations in a way that wouldn't alarm Guild readers if they checked his journal—framing his conflicted feelings as "processing the trauma of capture" rather than "planning eventual escape."
description.chat: Fire magic theory fills the pages, each lesson a step away from who you were and toward who you're becoming.

unidentified.name: Training Progress Journal
unidentified.description: A journal filled with detailed notes on magical training, including exercises, theoretical concepts, and instructor feedback. The handwriting shifts over time from frustrated scrawls to confident notation, documenting a learning process that appears to have been intensive and transformative. Personal reflections are mixed among the technical content, though their meaning isn't immediately clear.

A short wand of blackite—a volcanic glass found only in the deepest lava tubes of the Mushroom Kingdom's southern ranges—capped with a small ruby that pulses with inner fire. The Guild gave this to Dan after his third day of training, when his instructors recognized that his raw talent needed proper channeling tools rather than the makeshift focuses he'd been using. The wand doesn't increase his power, but it dramatically improves his control, allowing him to shape flames with precision that would have taken years to develop through practice alone.

Dan has mixed feelings about the wand. On one hand, it's the finest magical tool he's ever owned, crafted by Guild artificers specifically for fire magic and worth more gold than he'd seen in his entire life before the Vigilance. On the other hand, it's a leash as much as a gift—the wand is registered to the Guild, its magical signature tracked through their monitoring systems, and taking it outside Guild facilities without permission would trigger immediate pursuit. He's been told this is standard procedure for training equipment. He's been told he'll receive an unmarked wand of his own once he completes his associate period. He's been told a lot of things.

The wand grants a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls with fire spells and allows the wielder to add their proficiency bonus to damage rolls with cantrips that deal fire damage. It also functions as an arcane focus for all spellcasting.
description.chat: The ruby pulses in time with your heartbeat, hungry for the fire you're about to call.

unidentified.name: Volcanic Glass Wand
unidentified.description: A short wand of black volcanic glass capped with a small ruby that seems to contain actual flickering flames. The wand is warm to the touch, almost uncomfortably so, and leaves faint heat traces in the air when moved quickly. Something about it feels tracked, monitored, not entirely private.

A small brass badge bearing the number 447 and the Mages' Guild seal, issued to Dan as proof of his associate status within the organization. The badge is enchanted to glow faintly blue when within Guild facilities, confirming the wearer's authorized presence, and to burn uncomfortably hot if removed from the wearer without proper deactivation protocols. Dan learned about this second feature the hard way during his first attempt to leave it behind during a training exercise.

The badge also functions as a tracking device, allowing Guild administrators to monitor Dan's location within their facilities at all times. He's been told this is standard procedure for associates, a safety measure that ensures help can be dispatched quickly if training accidents occur. He's been told the tracking feature will be removed once he achieves full membership. He's been told many things that may or may not be true, and he's stopped trying to verify them all.

Wearing the badge openly marks Dan as someone operating under Guild authority. Hiding it marks him as someone the Guild should be concerned about. He's chosen to wear it openly, for now, while he gathers information and waits for the right moment to make a decision about his future.
description.chat: The brass badge gleams with your assigned number, marking you as property that hasn't quite been purchased yet.

unidentified.name: Numbered Brass Badge
unidentified.description: A small brass badge bearing a three-digit number and an official-looking seal. The badge glows faintly in certain lighting conditions and seems slightly warm to the touch. Attempting to remove it without knowing the proper technique would probably be a mistake.

A leather-bound spellbook provided by the Guild as part of Dan's training materials, containing a core curriculum of fire spells alongside utility magic deemed appropriate for an associate-level pyromancer. The book itself is new—Dan can still smell the fresh leather and binding glue—but the spells inside represent centuries of accumulated Guild knowledge, refined techniques that transform Dan's self-taught fire magic from dangerous improvisation into reliable, repeatable methodology.

The spellbook contains: Fire Bolt, Control Flames, Produce Flame (cantrips); Burning Hands, Chromatic Orb, Shield, Absorb Elements (1st level); Scorching Ray, Flaming Sphere, Misty Step (2nd level); Fireball, Counterspell, Dispel Magic (3rd level). The fire spells are extensively annotated with Guild instruction, including safety protocols, optimal gesture sequences, and warnings about common mistakes. The non-fire spells are presented with less commentary, practical additions that Dan's instructors deemed necessary for a well-rounded combat mage.

Dan has added his own notes in the margins, written in a personal shorthand he developed during his self-teaching years. Some notes are genuine observations about technique. Others are encoded reminders—supply cache locations, guard rotation patterns, things he's noticed about Guild operations that might prove useful if escape becomes necessary. The Guild instructors have seen him writing in the margins and approved of his "dedication to study." They have not decoded what he's actually recording.
description.chat: Pages crackle with residual heat as you turn them, each spell a lesson in controlled destruction.

unidentified.name: New Leather Spellbook
unidentified.description: A recently-bound spellbook in red leather with gold tooling, clearly of institutional quality. The pages are covered in formal spell notation with extensive instructional annotations, plus additional notes in a different hand—cramped, personal, sometimes encoded. Fire damage would be a logical concern for any book this close to flame magic, but the binding appears to be treated against heat.

Champion

Pursue Physical Excellence in Combat

A Champion focuses on the development of martial prowess in a relentless pursuit of victory. Champions combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows, withstand peril, and garner glory. Whether in athletic contests or bloody battle, Champions strive for the crown of the victor.

Level 3: Improved Critical

Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a @variantrule[Critical Hit|XPHB] on a roll of 19 or 20 on the [[/r d20]].

Level 3: Remarkable Athlete

Thanks to your athleticism, you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB] rolls and Strength (&Reference[skill=Athletics]) checks.

In addition, immediately after you score a @variantrule[Critical Hit|XPHB], you can move up to half your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] without provoking @action[Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks].

Level 7: Additional Fighting Style

You gain another Fighting Style feat of your choice.

Level 10: Heroic Warrior

The thrill of battle drives you toward victory. During combat, you can give yourself @variantrule[Heroic Inspiration|XPHB] whenever you start your turn without it.

Level 15: Superior Critical

Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can now score a @variantrule[Critical Hit|XPHB] on a roll of 18–20 on the [[/r d20]].

Level 18: Survivor

You attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle, giving you these benefits.

Defy Death. You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on @variantrule[Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws]. Moreover, when you roll 18–20 on a @variantrule[Death Saving Throw|XPHB], you gain the benefit of rolling a 20 on it.

Heroic Rally. At the start of each of your turns, you regain @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to 5 plus your Constitution modifier if you are @status[Bloodied|XPHB] and have at least 1 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point].
You gain another Fighting Style feat of your choice.

Fighting Style Feat (Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

When you're holding a Melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+)

You gain the following benefits.

Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Push. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals Bludgeoning damage, you can move it 5 feet to an unoccupied space if the target is no more than one size larger than you.

Enhanced Critical. When you score a @variantrule[Critical Hit|XPHB] that deals Bludgeoning damage to a creature, attack rolls against that creature have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] until the start of your next turn.

7th-level Rune Knight feature

You learn to invoke your rune magic to protect your allies. When another creature you can see within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to reroll the [[/r d20]] and use the new roll.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

The giant has a cloud rune inscribed on a mask in its possession. While holding or wearing the mask bearing the rune, the giant has truesight within a range of 30 feet and can use its Thunderous Clap action and Negate Spell reaction.

The mask bearing the cloud rune has AC 15; 45 hit points; and immunity to necrotic, poison, and psychic damage. The mask regains all its hit points at the end of every turn, but it turns to dust if reduced to 0 hit points or when the giant dies. If the rune is destroyed, the giant can inscribe a cloud rune on a mask in its possession when it finishes a short or long rest.

Your shell provides you a base AC of 17 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). This isn't just leathery hide; it is a tectonic plate of hardened keratin and scute, capable of deflecting broadswords, turning aside arrows, and withstanding the crushing pressure of a collapsing castle ceiling. The sheer thickness of Bowser's shell means he rarely needs to dodge; he simply lets the attacks shatter against his back.
